inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Strengthen Your Working Memory
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Strengthen Your Working Memory

What problem are we solving?

You know that feeling when your memory just goes blank in the middle of a question? And you kinda have no idea what you're supposed to do?

Yeah, that's not supposed to happen.

That's something to train out of you.

And this whole LSAT thing is going to feel so much better when you have the evidence you need to make the correct decisions in the moment. 

I never knew memory was such privilege and advantage. 

I used to think, "Of course everyone is subconsciously and instantaneously interrelating every answer choice with the compete conceptual idea behind the stimulus. That's the only way anyone would ever make a decision about an answer choice, right?"

WRONG.

This is the blindspot you have when you "just know" the answer to questions.

Choosing answers the way I just described feels so good that you can't imagine anyone would ever want to do it a different way.

But if you don't remember the complete conceptual idea behind the stimulus/passage while you're in the answer choices, you don't have the option of choosing answers this way.

That's the problem what we're here to solve.

This Accuracy Fix will train your memory to be able to enact this (much more fun and accurate) process in the answer choices.

Yes, the training is strenuous, but all good training is. And on the other side, you won't be able to believe you really chose answers without keeping the whole Translation in your working memory.

inline_prep.name: Stop Oversimplifying
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Stop Oversimplifying
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Stop Oversimplifying

What problem are we solving?

There is no such thing as "just a detail" on the LSAT. 

Ignoring "details" leads to missing question through oversimplifying. If you run with an inaccurate, oversimplified version of the text, you're bound to miss questions.

Answers are right and wrong based on "just one word." That doesn't make the LSAT mean, evil, or unfair. It makes the LSAT a test of precision.

And precision is something you'd to have when you're a lawyer, right? You don't want to be the attorney who harms their client because you missed "just one word." 

Every word on the LSAT deserves equal levels of respect, as it works with every other word to create a conceptual Translation of each sentence.

Conceptual Translation can be the single biggest differentiator between high and lower scorers. It is the opposite of oversimplifying. When you ignore some words in an answer choice and focus solely on other words (keywording), you're not conceptually translating that answer. You're oversimplifying and massively increasing your risk of missing the question.

Keywording reduces an answer's fate solely to whether it has certain words from the stimulus.

However, there are many correct answers that contain no words from the stimulus. There are many wrong answers that contain tons of words from the stimulus. 

You cannot oversimplify answer choice selection to a shallow matching game and expect the LSAT to tolerate it. It won't. 

But this is just one way oversimplification decreases your score. There are approximately one million other ways oversimplification decreases your score. 

This Accuracy Fix trains you to embrace complexity because your mind is strong enough to handle it. Luckily, this is something you were trained to do in the Translation Prep Stage. Now is the time to put that training into action, especially in the answer choices. 

That's how we stop you from missing so many questions.

inline_prep.name: Learn From Your Mistakes
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Learn From Your Mistakes
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Learn From Your Mistakes

What problem are we solving?

Seeing the score is like popping a balloon. 

You want to see the score so bad. Because you need to "see how you're doing," "understand where you are," "stay motivated," and "know what to work on."

So, of course, you need to check the score as soon as you're done with the section.  But suddenly, as soon as you see that number.

There's nothing interesting left anymore. 

Now you "know where you are," but the emotional reaction to where you are overwhelms any hope of strategic insights. 

If you like the number, you'll walk away excited and think, "Okay, now I'm good."

And then the next section is likely to crash and burn from laziness and complacency. You don't need to work that hard when you're good, right? 

If you don't like the number, tears follow.

Now there's no motivation to continue because nothing ever works. So what's the point? Why try? I should just give up and save the effort I would waste on this. I never get better. 

When you do this, you actively decline to change the behaviors that caused your wrong answers. This causes you to not improve.

Failing to look inward to understand what you need to change will cause you to leave points on the table.

This Accuracy Fix stops that rollercoaster of pain and plateaus.

You can get better. Give yourself the chance to really understand what you're doing wrong.

FIX 3 OF 7
Learn From Your Mistakes
What Problem Are We Solving?

Seeing the score is like popping a balloon. 

You want to see the score so bad. Because you need to "see how you're doing," "understand where you are," "stay motivated," and "know what to work on."

So, of course, you need to check the score as soon as you're done with the section.  But suddenly, as soon as you see that number.

There's nothing interesting left anymore. 

Now you "know where you are," but the emotional reaction to where you are overwhelms any hope of strategic insights. 

If you like the number, you'll walk away excited and think, "Okay, now I'm good."

And then the next section is likely to crash and burn from laziness and complacency. You don't need to work that hard when you're good, right? 

If you don't like the number, tears follow.

Now there's no motivation to continue because nothing ever works. So what's the point? Why try? I should just give up and save the effort I would waste on this. I never get better. 

When you do this, you actively decline to change the behaviors that caused your wrong answers. This causes you to not improve.

Failing to look inward to understand what you need to change will cause you to leave points on the table.

This Accuracy Fix stops that rollercoaster of pain and plateaus.

You can get better. Give yourself the chance to really understand what you're doing wrong.

sections.html:
Instructions

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

  1. For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

    1. Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

  2. For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

    1. Do not read the stimulus yet.

  3. For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

  4. Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

    1. After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

  5. Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

    1. Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

    2. Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

  6. Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • Mini-Cycles are great workouts for students with substantial previous prep experience.

    • They will force you to ditch toxic habits because they are so intentionally disruptive.

  • By slowing you down with radically different processes, Mini-Cycles force you to act with intention, rather than replaying old impulses just to go fast.

    • This often results in a significant accuracy gain for previously plateaued test takers.

  • Mini-Cycles are not meant to be done in 35 minutes, so do not rush this Workout to accommodate test-day timing. 50 minutes is considered a fast Mini-Cycle.

  • Don't let the fact that you are not confident in your ability to Party Trick ruin your Mini-Cycles.

    • No one is confident in their ability to Party Trick – it's not a Workout where you'll initially be sure of yourself.

    • The whole point of Party Tricking is that it makes you hone your intuition, which has discomfort attached to it in the beginning.

    • Choose an answer to the best of your Party-Tricking ability.

BACK
Mini-Cycle

Break every habit that's kept your score plateaued for too long

ADD TO MY STUFF
TELL ELLEN
CORE ACCURACY WORKOUTS
LR
ACCURACY
Quick Facts
Will This Help Me?

THIS WILL HELP YOU IF

You have bad habits from previous prep that you can't really enumerate, but you know you have to wipe the slate clean to ingrain new habits into your LSAT process.

Working on each skill individually feels like a more manageable task to you than putting everything together into a full section immediately

SKIP FOR NOW IF

You hate Party Tricking, so you're going to phone in the Party Trick stage of the drill. Go learn about Party Tricking to change your attitude.

CHALLENGE INDEX
Buckle Up
LEVEL
Intermediate
MINIMUM TIME
53+ minutes
TIMING COMPATIBLE WITH
53m, 70m, Natural Pace, Marathon
Instructions

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

VIDEO WALKTHROUGH

How and Why to Do a Mini-Cycle

SECTIONS TO USE

New Sections Only

HOW TO TIME

Count-Up Stopwatch

Countdown Timer

Ellen's Advice
If You Want to Win

Mini-Cycles are great workouts for students with substantial previous prep experience.

They will force you to ditch toxic habits because they are so intentionally disruptive.

By slowing you down with radically different processes, Mini-Cycles force you to act with intention, rather than replaying old impulses just to go fast.

This often results in a significant accuracy gain for previously plateaued test takers.

Mini-Cycles are not meant to be done in 35 minutes, so do not rush this Workout to accommodate test-day timing. 50 minutes is considered a fast Mini-Cycle.

Don't let the fact that you are not confident in your ability to Party Trick ruin your Mini-Cycles.

No one is confident in their ability to Party Trick – it's not a Workout where you'll initially be sure of yourself.

The whole point of Party Tricking is that it makes you hone your intuition, which has discomfort attached to it in the beginning.

Choose an answer to the best of your Party-Tricking ability.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
What Problem Are We Solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
What Problem Are We Solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • It is very important that you do not take breaks between sections or check your sections in the middle of the Marathon.

    • Marathons only work because your brain doesn’t get the chance to re-adapt to non-LSAT thinking.

    • Taking breaks guarantees that the Marathon will not work.

      • Do not check your phone.

      • Do not have conversations.

      • Do not take a lunch break.

    • Put snacks and drinks on the desk to eat while you Marathon, if needed.

    • The only breaks allowed during Marathons are medically required or biologically required breaks.

      • Running to the bathroom is allowed between sections.

      • Accommodated breaks for medically required tasks (like insulin injections, etc) are obviously allowed.

  • Open all the sections you plan to complete in separate tabs before starting the Marathon.

  • It is exceptionally important that you do not see the score of each section in the middle of the Marathon.

    • If you see the scores, it will take out of the focused activity and all the intuition-building work will be undone. The Marathon will be wasted.

  • Marathons should be performed on only one type of section at a time unless otherwise specified (as in, Mixed Section Marathons).

    • This means that all the sections of the Marathon are LR, or all the sections of the Marathon are RC.

  • Keep track of the order of the sections in your Marathon, so you can analyze the results.

  • If you feel yourself getting worse as the Marathon progresses, you are likely becoming fatigued.

    • This is ok, but it indicates that you’ll need to do another Marathon. Fatigue is part of the process; it indicates that you need to build stamina.

  • At the end of the Marathon, take a break and then Camo all the sections in a big batch.

Timing Tips

How Marathon Timing Works

  • Use a stopwatch and a 35-minute countdown timer on LawHub to time your sections.

    • In LawHub, use Self-Paced Mode. Do not use Exam Mode.

    • If you have extended time, change the 35-minute countdown timer to the amount of time you have to complete the section according to your accommodations.

  • If the countdown timer runs out and you are not done, write down what question you were on when time ran out. Continue the section until you finish, and write down the time it took you to finish as soon as you finish it.

    • Just look down at the stopwatch when you finish it and write down what you see.

  • Keep track of the timed and untimed score after you review.

  • Do not pretend that Marathon timing is the same as test-day timing.

    • Do not do all the Marathon sections with bad form in order to meet test-day timing before you're ready. It is expected that you first few Marathons will contain sections that go far beyond the test-day time limit.

    • Pretending that you're ready for test-day timed sections before you're actually ready for them (finishing Marathons within the test-day time limit even though this deeply hurts your accuracy) will only ingrain bad form and make you significantly worse. I don't want to hurt you, so PLEASE do not do this. Let the Marathon sections take longer than test-day timed sections, if they need to in order to maintain the accuracy.

  • If you are consistently finishing your Marathon sections within 35 minutes (or 36/37 minutes) and your accuracy is suffering, do your Marathons with a stopwatch only and no countdown timer. Set LawHub to 400 minutes at the start of each section so the timer doesn't bother you.

Get started with speed and stamina training

ADD TO MY STUFF
TELL ELLEN
MARATHONS
RC/LR
SPEED
Quick Facts
Will This Help Me?

THIS WILL HELP YOU IF

You need to get faster but don't have the stamina for a full Marathon yet, or you're nervous about starting Marathon training, so you want to start off with a more accessible drill first.

SKIP FOR NOW IF

You have persistent accuracy problems that you do not yet understand.

CHALLENGE INDEX
Ellen Whyyy
LEVEL
Intermediate
MINIMUM TIME
175+ minutes
TIMING COMPATIBLE WITH
Marathon
Instructions
Complete five LR sections* in one sitting with no breaks, or complete five RC sections in one sitting with no breaks.

VIDEO WALKTHROUGH

How and Why to Marathon

SECTIONS TO USE

Mix in Previously Seen Sections

HOW TO TIME

Count-Up Stopwatch

Countdown Timer

Ellen's Advice
If You Want to Win

It is very important that you do not take breaks between sections or check your sections in the middle of the Marathon.

Marathons only work because your brain doesn’t get the chance to re-adapt to non-LSAT thinking.

Taking breaks guarantees that the Marathon will not work.

Do not check your phone.

Do not have conversations.

Do not take a lunch break.

Put snacks and drinks on the desk to eat while you Marathon, if needed.

The only breaks allowed during Marathons are medically required or biologically required breaks.

Running to the bathroom is allowed between sections.

Accommodated breaks for medically required tasks (like insulin injections, etc) are obviously allowed.

Open all the sections you plan to complete in separate tabs before starting the Marathon.

It is exceptionally important that you do not see the score of each section in the middle of the Marathon.

If you see the scores, it will take out of the focused activity and all the intuition-building work will be undone. The Marathon will be wasted.

Marathons should be performed on only one type of section at a time unless otherwise specified (as in, Mixed Section Marathons).

This means that all the sections of the Marathon are LR, or all the sections of the Marathon are RC.

Keep track of the order of the sections in your Marathon, so you can analyze the results.

If you feel yourself getting worse as the Marathon progresses, you are likely becoming fatigued.

This is ok, but it indicates that you’ll need to do another Marathon. Fatigue is part of the process; it indicates that you need to build stamina.

At the end of the Marathon, take a break and then Camo all the sections in a big batch.

SHOW LESS
Timing Tips

How Marathon Timing Works

Use a stopwatch and a 35-minute countdown timer on LawHub to time your sections.

In LawHub, use Self-Paced Mode. Do not use Exam Mode.

If you have extended time, change the 35-minute countdown timer to the amount of time you have to complete the section according to your accommodations.

If the countdown timer runs out and you are not done, write down what question you were on when time ran out. Continue the section until you finish, and write down the time it took you to finish as soon as you finish it.

Just look down at the stopwatch when you finish it and write down what you see.

Keep track of the timed and untimed score after you review.

Do not pretend that Marathon timing is the same as test-day timing.

Do not do all the Marathon sections with bad form in order to meet test-day timing before you're ready. It is expected that you first few Marathons will contain sections that go far beyond the test-day time limit.

Pretending that you're ready for test-day timed sections before you're actually ready for them (finishing Marathons within the test-day time limit even though this deeply hurts your accuracy) will only ingrain bad form and make you significantly worse. I don't want to hurt you, so PLEASE do not do this. Let the Marathon sections take longer than test-day timed sections, if they need to in order to maintain the accuracy.

If you are consistently finishing your Marathon sections within 35 minutes (or 36/37 minutes) and your accuracy is suffering, do your Marathons with a stopwatch only and no countdown timer. Set LawHub to 400 minutes at the start of each section so the timer doesn't bother you.

SHOW LESS
Real Examples

Section Data to Track

During section on your scratch paper, write down:

The amount of extra time needed to finish the section, if applicable

The number of the last question you answered before test-day time expired

After Camo, record in your tracker:

Test-day timed score

Extra-time score

Camo score

Mini-Marathon Routine

Why are we doing this?

Mini-Marathon Routines are a great introduction to speed training, but they are less effective at reducing time than full Marathon Routines.

The purpose of starting Speed practice with Mini-Marathon Routines is to gradually build up the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, which will allow us to both get faster and exceed the stamina requirements of test day.

If you've been doing Translation + CLIR and Decaf Marathons, you may already have the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, in which case you can skip this Speed Routine and begin Marathon Routines immediately.

How to Pull This Off

Marathon Routine Protocols

  • Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

    • If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

  • Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

    • The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

  • Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

  • Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

    • This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

  • Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How to move on

Once Mini-Marathons are no longer exhausting, or they are only exhausting on the last section, it's time to move on to a full Marathon Routine.

If you're still not hitting both your time and accuracy goals, or you're only just starting to reach those goals on one or two sections in the Mini-Marathon, progress to a full Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Mini-Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • It is very important that you do not take breaks between sections or check your sections in the middle of the Marathon.

    • Marathons only work because your brain doesn’t get the chance to re-adapt to non-LSAT thinking.

    • Taking breaks guarantees that the Marathon will not work.

      • Do not check your phone.

      • Do not have conversations.

      • Do not take a lunch break.

    • Put snacks and drinks on the desk to eat while you Marathon, if needed.

    • The only breaks allowed during Marathons are medically required or biologically required breaks.

      • Running to the bathroom is allowed between sections.

      • Accommodated breaks for medically required tasks (like insulin injections, etc) are obviously allowed.

  • Open all the sections you plan to complete in separate tabs before starting the Marathon.

  • It is exceptionally important that you do not see the score of each section in the middle of the Marathon.

    • If you see the scores, it will take out of the focused activity and all the intuition-building work will be undone. The Marathon will be wasted.

  • Keep track of the order of the sections in your Marathon, so you can analyze the results.

  • If you feel yourself getting worse as the Marathon progresses, you are likely becoming fatigued.

    • This is ok, but it indicates that you’ll need to do another Marathon. Fatigue is part of the process; it indicates that you need to build stamina.

  • At the end of the Marathon, take a break and then Camo all the sections in a big batch.

Timing Tips

How Marathon Timing Works

  • Use a stopwatch and a 35-minute countdown timer on LawHub to time your sections.

    • In LawHub, use Self-Paced Mode. Do not use Exam Mode.

    • If you have extended time, change the 35-minute countdown timer to the amount of time you have to complete the section according to your accommodations.

  • If the countdown timer runs out and you are not done, write down what question you were on when time ran out. Continue the section until you finish, and write down the time it took you to finish as soon as you finish it.

    • Just look down at the stopwatch when you finish it and write down what you see.

  • Keep track of the timed and untimed score after you review.

  • Do not pretend that Marathon timing is the same as test-day timing.

    • Do not do all the Marathon sections with bad form in order to meet test-day timing before you're ready. It is expected that you first few Marathons will contain sections that go far beyond the test-day time limit.

    • Pretending that you're ready for test-day timed sections before you're actually ready for them (finishing Marathons within the test-day time limit even though this deeply hurts your accuracy) will only ingrain bad form and make you significantly worse. I don't want to hurt you, so PLEASE do not do this. Let the Marathon sections take longer than test-day timed sections, if they need to in order to maintain the accuracy.

  • If you are consistently finishing your Marathon sections within 35 minutes (or 36/37 minutes) and your accuracy is suffering, do your Marathons with a stopwatch only and no countdown timer. Set LawHub to 400 minutes at the start of each section so the timer doesn't bother you.

Mixed Section Marathon Routine

Why are we doing this?

Mixed Section Marathon Routines are fantastic for students who struggle with context switching and stamina.

If you have any worry about being depleted during the last section on test day, Mixed Section Marathons are better than PTs and standard Marathons for stamina training.

After you've done 1.5x to 2x the sections of a PT in a single sitting with no breaks, it will feel like nothing to do four sections on test day with a break between sections 1 and 2.

How to Pull This Off

Mixed Section Marathons should be approached similarly to regular Marathons, so be sure to familiarize yourself with the Marathon timing procedures, section data to track, and advice on how to win contained in the Marathon Workout instructions.

Marathon Routine Protocols

  • Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

    • If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

  • Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

    • The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

  • Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

  • Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

    • This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

  • Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How to move on

Mixed Section Marathons are not the most effective Routines for reducing time.

If you are still having trouble meeting you test-day timing goal, you should progress to another Speed Routine that is more suited to pure time reduction (like the Marathon Routine or the Failsafe Marathon Routine).

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Mixed Section Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

sections.html:
Instructions

  1. Complete six to eight LR sections* in one sitting with no breaks, or complete six to eight RC sections in one sitting with no breaks.

  2. Alternate test-day timed sections with Marathon-timed sections throughout the Marathon.

    1. This means, on the first section of the Marathon, you will move on to the next section immediately once your LawHub section timer expires (no extra time).

    2. On the next section, you will follow the Marathon timing procedures noted in the Marathon instructions.

    3. You can choose to alternate the test-day timed sections and Marathon-timed sections in any pattern you want.

    4. For instance, it may be useful to alternate every two sections of test-day timing with one section of Marathon timing (2:1:2:1:2).

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • It is very important that you do not take breaks between sections or check your sections in the middle of the Marathon.

    • Marathons only work because your brain doesn’t get the chance to re-adapt to non-LSAT thinking.

    • Taking breaks guarantees that the Marathon will not work.

      • Do not check your phone.

      • Do not have conversations.

      • Do not take a lunch break.

    • Put snacks and drinks on the desk to eat while you Marathon, if needed.

    • The only breaks allowed during Marathons are medically required or biologically required breaks

      • Running to the bathroom is allowed between sections.

      • Accommodated breaks for medically required tasks (like insulin injections, etc) are obviously allowed.

  • Open all the sections you plan to complete in separate tabs before starting the Marathon.

  • It is exceptionally important that you do not see the score of each section in the middle of the Marathon.

    • If you see the scores, it will take out of the focused activity and all the intuition-building work will be undone. The Marathon will be wasted.

  • Marathons should be performed on only one type of section at a time unless otherwise specified (as in, Mixed Section Marathons).

    • This means that all the sections of the Marathon are LR, or all the sections of the Marathon are RC.

  • Keep track of the order of the sections in your Marathon, so you can analyze the results.

  • If you feel yourself getting worse as the Marathon progresses, you are likely becoming fatigued.

    • This is ok, but it indicates that you’ll need to do another Marathon. Fatigue is part of the process; it indicates that you need to build stamina.

  • At the end of the Marathon, take a break and then Camo all the sections in a big batch.

Timing Tips

  • For your test-day timed sections, set a section timer for test-day timing in LawHub's Self-Paced Mode.

    • Do not use LawHub's Exam Mode.

  • For your Marathon-timed sections, follow the timing protocols outlined in the Marathon Timing Tips.

inline_prep.name: Mixed Timing Marathon Routine
inline_prep.html:
Speed
Mixed Timing Marathon Routine
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Speed

Mixed Timing Marathon Routine

Why are we doing this?

The purpose of Mixed Timing Marathon Routines is to gradually integrate test-day timing standards into your skillset while minimally disrupting accuracy.

By allowing alternation between Marathon timing and test-day timing, you have the opportunity to reaffirm your standards without compromise during the Marathon-timed sections and then get used to pushing those standards into the test-day timing window.

Don't attempt Mixed Timing Marathon Routines if your marathon-timed sections are 10+ minutes from test-day timing.

Mixed Timing Marathons are not typically as effective as regular Marathons at large time reduction (10+ minutes) since the alternation makes it more difficult to reach the flow state required for subconscious skill integration (which is what allows the time to drop).

However, Mixed Timing Marathons are great to ease into how test day will feel.

LR
RC

Challenge IndexBuckle Up
LevelAdvanced
Study block4-5+ hours
Time goal to move on20 min

Routine Schedule

Do these workouts in this order. For real, the order matters.

How to Pull This Off

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

  • Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

    • If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

  • Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

    • The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

  • Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

  • Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

    • This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

  • Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How to move on

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How To Move On

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • We want high information density in what we learn from the answer choices and question stems

    • We don't want "There is research about platypus"

    • We want "There is scientific research on the function of a platypus' bill, potentially to locate prey"

  • Make sure the things you learn from each question and answer choice is new and distinct

  • Make sure you're not simplifying the nouns (don't change neocortex to cortex)

  • When you hit a question with a ton of scientific jargon, treat it as a preview of what will happen in the passage.

    • You now know that you are going to be responsible for these nouns and verbs, so learn as much as you possibly can able these words

  • Give yourself a shot to quip in a ton of depth on each of the answer choices to interrelate the content of the answers on previous questions

    • This will allow you to put together the pieces to understand the story of the question.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Stop Mental and Physical Self-Sabotage
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Stop Mental and Physical Self-Sabotage

What problem are we solving?

Have you ever done a section when:

  • you're falling asleep in the middle? 

  • someone else is taking a call a little too close to you? 

  • you're looking at the clock over and over again and saying to yourself "I have to speed up"?

  • you're saying to yourself, "I can't get this wrong. Oh my god, I don't understand. I have to get it. I'll never get into Berkeley. My dad is right about me."?

  • you just saw a previous score and you're going to cry?

  • you have a stye on your left eye and also maybe COVID?

Doing the LSAT like this is mental and physical self-sabotage.

You are willfully engaging in behaviors that decrease your score. 

I care about you and I care about your score, so I'm going to give you some real talk here.

Telling yourself you can't do something drastically increases the chances you won't be able to do that thing.

So stop it. 

Doing LSAT in an environment or situation that pulls on your attention sets you up to fail.

So stop it.

Thinking about the past, the future, and what other people think while you're doing the LSAT ensures that you do not do your best.

So stop it.

This is your Olympics.

We need you in peak mental and physical condition while you're training to ensure that you're in peak condition on test day. This means that you have to advocate for yourself.

Create space in your life for LSAT is to be the #1 priority, not something you do after every high priority is done.

This Accuracy Fix teaches you how to be that your advocate.

  1. Prep Map/

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

sections.html:
Instructions

  1. Set the LawHub to 400 minutes in Self-Paced Mode*.

    1. This is to make sure the LawHub timer doesn't interfere with your natural pace.

  2. Start a stopwatch.

  3. Complete your first pass through the section.

  4. Press Lap on the stopwatch.

    1. On iPhone, the Lap button is labeled "Lap."

    2. On Android, the Lap button has a stopwatch symbol and is to the right of the Pause button.

  5. Complete your hyperskip pass.

  6. Stop the stopwatch.

  7. Record the lap times and total time.

    1. The first lap time is your first-pass time. This tells us how long it took you to answer the questions.

    2. The second lap time is your hyperskip time. This tells us how long your hyperskip pass took.

    3. Your total time is how long you took on the section in total. This is your natural pace.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • Natural Pace sections are adaptable to any Workout. You can think of them like a modification on how any Workout is timed.

    • For instance, you can do a Natural Pace section on a Mini-Cycle, Inside Out, or Acronym.

    • Since Natural Pace sections only specify how the Workout is timed, they overlay on any other Workout.

  • Natural Pace sections are great for fixing accuracy issues without the pressure of time.

  • If you struggle with anxiety, you'll want to primarily focus on Natural Pace sections in the beginning of your prep until you start to feel comfortable with the exam.

    • You can work to bring your time down gradually through Marathons, Failsafes, and Pacing Practice later.

  • If you have a stop/start breaks accommodation, you can take breaks during section by pressing Pause on the stopwatch.

    • Put a Post-It over the time display on the stopwatch so you can't see the amount of time that's passed when you press Pause.

inline_prep.name: Intuition, Not Impulse
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse

Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
What Problem Are We Solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

sections.html:
Instructions

  1. Choose an interval time goal.

    1. Your interval time goal is your target time for each question.

    2. For example, an interval time goal may be 90 seconds per question.

    3. Follow the procedures of How to Set a Realistic Interval Time Goal below.

  2. Set an interval timer to repeatedly countdown from that time goal 30 times in a row.

    1. Do not incorporate rest intervals.

    2. We choose 30 times so we can have some extra intervals in case our timer messes up.

  3. Start your interval timer when you begin an LR or RC section*.

    1. For RC, only use the interval timer on the questions, not during the passage.

  4. You must select an answer on each question before the interval timer goes off.

    1. You cannot stay on a question longer than the interval timer permits, no matter how badly you want to.

  • Pacing Practice trains you to pace yourself.

    • It is an ideal workout if you find yourself over-investing in a few questions throughout the section and, in doing so, causing yourself to run out of time.

  • You can use Pacing Practice within a test-day timed section just to ensure that you're moving on when you should, or you can use Pacing Practice on stopwatch-timed sections to gradually introduce timing in a controlled environment.

    • It's a versatile workout with many applications, so enjoy adapting it to your needs.

Timing Tips

To Set a Realistic Interval Time Goal

  • Start with your natural pace and divide that natural pace by the number of questions in a section. This result is your interval time per question.

    • Your natural pace is how long it takes you to complete a section at goal accuracy without worrying about the time.

    • For instance, if your natural pace is 50 minutes per section and you divide that by the number of questions in a given LR section (~25 questions), you would have an interval time goal of 2 minutes per question.

  • If your natural pace time is above your test-day time, gradually lower your interval time by 3-10 seconds after every Pacing Practice that meets your accuracy goal

    • Keep lowering the interval time until your interval time goes below your test-day timing.

Instructions

Choose an interval time goal.

Your interval time goal is your target time for each question.

For example, an interval time goal may be 90 seconds per question.

Follow the procedures of How to Set a Realistic Interval Time Goal below.

Set an interval timer to repeatedly countdown from that time goal 30 times in a row.

Do not incorporate rest intervals.

We choose 30 times so we can have some extra intervals in case our timer messes up.

Start your interval timer when you begin an LR or RC section*.

For RC, only use the interval timer on the questions, not during the passage.

You must select an answer on each question before the interval timer goes off.

You cannot stay on a question longer than the interval timer permits, no matter how badly you want to.

  1. Prep Map/

Timing Failsafe Routine

Why are we doing this?

Timing Failsafe Routines are one of the only ways to effectively reduce time without Marathoning.

The upsides of Timing Failsafes are:

  • They can be done in shorter periods of time than a Marathon

  • They allow for more systematic gradual time reduction

  • Review can be more targeted and frequent

This Routine works great for students who thrive on structure.

How to Pull This Off

Failsafe Routines work best when combined with other Routines to bring time down while maintaining accuracy.

Essentially, you have to address the reasons why the Failsafe breaks in order to get it to progress, so you'll want to consider alternating Failsafe Routines with the Accuracy Fix Routines that pertain to your mistakes.

How to move on

Timing Failsafe Routines can get you to test-day goal time and accuracy without progressing to any other Speed Routine.

However, if you have lost every Timing Failsafe you've attempted for three consecutive prep days, here are a few options for what you can try next:

  1. Set a higher baseline natural pace to start your Timing Failsafe

  2. Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with a Light Failsafe

  3. Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with Pacing Practice

  4. Return to the Accuracy Fix Routines

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Timing Failsafes, progress to any of the following Speed Routines: Failsafe Marathon Routine, Mini-Marathon Routine, or Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Timing Failsafe Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

Instructions

NOTE: Party Trick Circles are an advanced workout. Do not attempt Party Trick Circles until you have completed a few sections of Party Tricking Jail.

  1. Party Trick the answer choices*.

  2. Translate, quip, and CLIR the stimulus.

  3. Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

  4. On each individual answer choice:

    1. Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

    2. Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

      1. If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

      2. If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

      3. If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

  5. Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

  6. Hyperskip, if needed.

    1. Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

  7. Reattempt your hyperskips according to the LR Full Question Process, not the Party Trick Circle Process.

Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • Party Trick Circles fundamentally alter your perception of difficulty in Logical Reasoning.

    • The questions feel so different (and often so much easier) when you Party Trick them first.

  • Party Trick Circles can be a great way to break a plateau on LR.

  • It can be difficult to ensure that you properly CLIR and Mission on Party Trick Circles because the subconscious recognition of the correct answer can be involuntary, even while you're still in the middle of the stimulus.

    • Stay strong in your process.

    • Don't get too hasty and miss questions because you didn't give every answer a proper post-stimulus chance.

inline_prep.name: Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Don't Be Desperate in the Answers

What problem are we solving?

Sometimes you just want to get the question right so badly that every answer choice looks like an escape hatch.

"Is it right? Is it right!??

If it's right, then I can move on.

Then I won't waste any more time.

Then the stimulus must have meant this.

Then this must have been what they were looking for."

Notice the desperation dripping off this monologue. 

You're looking for an answer choice to rescue you, but actually the roles need to be reversed. You have to be the strong one.

Be for real. You are better than 80% wrong. 

Answer choices are designed to exploit your desire for them to be right and to prey on moments of inattention.

But you can channel your desire to get the question right into building an invulnerable fortress of analysis throughout every stage of the question. This fortress (Translation, CLIR, Mission, Back Up Plan) will allow you to see exactly why these answers are wrong without. any. drama.

The answer choices only gain manipulative power over you when you look to them to save you. But you are not the freaking damsel that answer C is here to rescue. You're the hero.

You're here to judge answer C, and you're going to judge it according to your vetted, bulletproof standards.

The answers need to impress you, not the other way around.

This Accuracy Fix trains you to build the fortress.

Because you are smart enough. You have the tools, the time, and the resources to never need any answer choice to save you again.

FIX 6 OF 7
Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
What Problem Are We Solving?

Sometimes you just want to get the question right so badly that every answer choice looks like an escape hatch.

"Is it right? Is it right!??

If it's right, then I can move on.

Then I won't waste any more time.

Then the stimulus must have meant this.

Then this must have been what they were looking for."

Notice the desperation dripping off this monologue. 

You're looking for an answer choice to rescue you, but actually the roles need to be reversed. You have to be the strong one.

Be for real. You are better than 80% wrong. 

Answer choices are designed to exploit your desire for them to be right and to prey on moments of inattention.

But you can channel your desire to get the question right into building an invulnerable fortress of analysis throughout every stage of the question. This fortress (Translation, CLIR, Mission, Back Up Plan) will allow you to see exactly why these answers are wrong without. any. drama.

The answer choices only gain manipulative power over you when you look to them to save you. But you are not the freaking damsel that answer C is here to rescue. You're the hero.

You're here to judge answer C, and you're going to judge it according to your vetted, bulletproof standards.

The answers need to impress you, not the other way around.

This Accuracy Fix trains you to build the fortress.

Because you are smart enough. You have the tools, the time, and the resources to never need any answer choice to save you again.

sections.html:
Instructions

NOTE: Party Tricking Jail is an advanced workout for those who want to push themselves to become true answer choice experts. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before entering Party Tricking Jail.

  1. Party Trick every question in an LR or RC section*.

    1. This means you will only read the question stem and answer choices on each question before you select an answer on that question.

    2. Do not look at the stimulus or passage.

  2. Camo the section immediately after completing it.

    1. The Camo will display all the questions that are wrong plus an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

    2. Do not look at the stimulus when you Camo.

    3. Party Trick the returned questions again. Doubt your answers on the questions Camo displays and try to correct your answer.

  3. Get as close to -0 on the Camo as you can.

  4. OPTIONAL: Do not exit Party Tricking Jail until you reach -5 or better pre-Camo.

    1. You can customize this accuracy goal to your personal needs.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • Traditionally, Party Tricking Jail has been assigned when an advanced student reaches a score plateau around -3 to -6,

    • I'll assign Party Tricking Jail when the plateau results from inadequate answer choice processing.

    • When I assign Party Tricking Jail this way, I suspend all the student's other homework so their entire Routine is only Party Tricking Jail.

    • I find it effective to suspend all the other homework so the student is more able to break the old habits that have left them plateaued.

    • However, you do not have to complete Party Tricking Jail as the only Workout in your Routine.

  • Party Tricking Jail should not be undertaken unless you can pass Level 5 of MemAC or have a true appetite for danger.

    • If you're not sensitive about being unsure, feel free to try Party Tricking Jail and learn about Party Tricking as you go.

  • It's key to push past the first few questions of Party Tricking Jail where you will undoubtedly feel uncertain and potentially uncomfortable.

    • Feeling uncertain is the whole point.

    • This is a Workout that is designed to hone your intuition. Like Arya learning to fight with a blindfold on.

BACK
Party Tricking Jail

Train your intuition to get questions right without even reading the stimulus or passage

ADD TO MY STUFF
TELL ELLEN
PARTY TRICKING
RC/LR
ACCURACY
Quick Facts
Will This Help Me?

THIS WILL HELP YOU IF

You don't have expert-level intuition in the answer choices and you want to gain that intuition in order to up-level your speed and accuracy.

SKIP FOR NOW IF

You haven't completed the Answer Choice Translation Primer, and you haven't beaten Level Five of MemAC.

You aren't bought into the Party Tricking, so you rush through the process, repeating that you don't know. Go learn about Party Tricking to change your attitude.

CHALLENGE INDEX
Buckle Up
LEVEL
Advanced
MINIMUM TIME
35+ minutes
TIMING COMPATIBLE WITH
Stopwatch
Instructions

NOTE: Party Tricking Jail is an advanced workout for those who want to push themselves to become true answer choice experts. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before entering Party Tricking Jail.

Party Trick every question in an LR or RC section*.

This means you will only read the question stem and answer choices on each question before you select an answer on that question.

Do not look at the stimulus or passage.

Camo the section immediately after completing it.

The Camo will display all the questions that are wrong plus an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Do not look at the stimulus when you Camo.

Party Trick the returned questions again. Doubt your answers on the questions Camo displays and try to correct your answer.

Get as close to -0 on the Camo as you can.

OPTIONAL: Do not exit Party Tricking Jail until you reach -5 or better pre-Camo.

You can customize this accuracy goal to your personal needs.

VIDEO WALKTHROUGH

How and Why to Enter Party Tricking Jail

SECTIONS TO USE

Ideal for Previously Seen Sections

HOW TO TIME

Count-Up Stopwatch

Ellen's Advice
If You Want to Win

Traditionally, Party Tricking Jail has been assigned when an advanced student reaches a score plateau around -3 to -6,

I'll assign Party Tricking Jail when the plateau results from inadequate answer choice processing.

When I assign Party Tricking Jail this way, I suspend all the student's other homework so their entire Routine is only Party Tricking Jail.

I find it effective to suspend all the other homework so the student is more able to break the old habits that have left them plateaued.

However, you do not have to complete Party Tricking Jail as the only Workout in your Routine.

Party Tricking Jail should not be undertaken unless you can pass Level 5 of MemAC or have a true appetite for danger.

If you're not sensitive about being unsure, feel free to try Party Tricking Jail and learn about Party Tricking as you go.

It's key to push past the first few questions of Party Tricking Jail where you will undoubtedly feel uncertain and potentially uncomfortable.

Feeling uncertain is the whole point.

This is a Workout that is designed to hone your intuition. Like Arya learning to fight with a blindfold on.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Don't Be Desperate in the Answers

What problem are we solving?

Sometimes you just want to get the question right so badly that every answer choice looks like an escape hatch.

"Is it right? Is it right!??

If it's right, then I can move on.

Then I won't waste any more time.

Then the stimulus must have meant this.

Then this must have been what they were looking for."

Notice the desperation dripping off this monologue. 

You're looking for an answer choice to rescue you, but actually the roles need to be reversed. You have to be the strong one.

Be for real. You are better than 80% wrong. 

Answer choices are designed to exploit your desire for them to be right and to prey on moments of inattention.

But you can channel your desire to get the question right into building an invulnerable fortress of analysis throughout every stage of the question. This fortress (Translation, CLIR, Mission, Back Up Plan) will allow you to see exactly why these answers are wrong without. any. drama.

The answer choices only gain manipulative power over you when you look to them to save you. But you are not the freaking damsel that answer C is here to rescue. You're the hero.

You're here to judge answer C, and you're going to judge it according to your vetted, bulletproof standards.

The answers need to impress you, not the other way around.

This Accuracy Fix trains you to build the fortress.

Because you are smart enough. You have the tools, the time, and the resources to never need any answer choice to save you again.

inline_prep.name: Strengthen Your Working Memory
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Strengthen Your Working Memory
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Strengthen Your Working Memory

What problem are we solving?

You know that feeling when your memory just goes blank in the middle of a question? And you kinda have no idea what you're supposed to do?

Yeah, that's not supposed to happen.

That's something to train out of you.

And this whole LSAT thing is going to feel so much better when you have the evidence you need to make the correct decisions in the moment. 

I never knew memory was such privilege and advantage. 

I used to think, "Of course everyone is subconsciously and instantaneously interrelating every answer choice with the compete conceptual idea behind the stimulus. That's the only way anyone would ever make a decision about an answer choice, right?"

WRONG.

This is the blindspot you have when you "just know" the answer to questions.

Choosing answers the way I just described feels so good that you can't imagine anyone would ever want to do it a different way.

But if you don't remember the complete conceptual idea behind the stimulus/passage while you're in the answer choices, you don't have the option of choosing answers this way.

That's the problem what we're here to solve.

This Accuracy Fix will train your memory to be able to enact this (much more fun and accurate) process in the answer choices.

Yes, the training is strenuous, but all good training is. And on the other side, you won't be able to believe you really chose answers without keeping the whole Translation in your working memory.

sections.html:
Instructions

Any question you'd pose to me (real Ellen), you can pose to AI Ellen. Since she's my AI clone, she can be wrong, but she does a pretty great job most of the time. I read the questions you pose to AI Ellen and will often fine-tune AI Ellen's response when it differs from I would say.

Here are a few things she can do that you might want to try out:

  • Use AI Ellen as your daily LSAT journaling partner. Keep her updated on your progress and she can help you keep track of everything you've done.

  • She can answer your questions about the Loophole Online videos and about the Loophole book.

  • She can make you a quiz on question stem identification, explain why your answer was wrong, and then adapt the quiz to concentrate on your weaknesses.

  • She can quiz you on premise indicators, conclusion indicators, conditional indicators, and causal indicators. She can then requiz you only on the indicators you don't reliably know.

  • She can listen to all your anxiety thoughts about the LSAT and give you strategies that can help you on test day and in your prep.

sections.html:
Real Examples

To Practice Conditional Reasoning

  • PROMPT: I want you to help me practice my conditional diagramming skills. Make me fun examples that look like real LSAT stimuli. Present these examples to me one at a time. I will attempt to diagram each example you give me or tell you the example can't be diagrammed. Make the examples difficult. Mix up the order of the conditional phrases, so they don't always start off the same way. Never draw Must Arrows pointed to the left. Do not include any examples that chain conditionals off of and/or conditions. Use a wide variety of conditional indicators in the examples, include Some, Most, Not All, or Few in 20% of the examples. 5% of your examples should not include any conditionals. Include Include or Exclusion indicators in 10% of the examples. Include "only if" in 10% of the examples. Include conditional chaining in 50% of the examples. Allow for inferencing with Some/Most chains on 10% of the examples. Check to make sure I identify the Three Valid Some/Most Inferences when they appear. Always give me feedback on my responses to help me improve my conditional diagramming skills and show me how to diagram the example correctly. Be encouraging since conditional diagramming is difficult.

inline_prep.name: Strengthen Your Working Memory
inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Strengthen Your Working Memory
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Strengthen Your Working Memory

What problem are we solving?

You know that feeling when your memory just goes blank in the middle of a question? And you kinda have no idea what you're supposed to do?

Yeah, that's not supposed to happen.

That's something to train out of you.

And this whole LSAT thing is going to feel so much better when you have the evidence you need to make the correct decisions in the moment. 

I never knew memory was such privilege and advantage. 

I used to think, "Of course everyone is subconsciously and instantaneously interrelating every answer choice with the compete conceptual idea behind the stimulus. That's the only way anyone would ever make a decision about an answer choice, right?"

WRONG.

This is the blindspot you have when you "just know" the answer to questions.

Choosing answers the way I just described feels so good that you can't imagine anyone would ever want to do it a different way.

But if you don't remember the complete conceptual idea behind the stimulus/passage while you're in the answer choices, you don't have the option of choosing answers this way.

That's the problem what we're here to solve.

This Accuracy Fix will train your memory to be able to enact this (much more fun and accurate) process in the answer choices.

Yes, the training is strenuous, but all good training is. And on the other side, you won't be able to believe you really chose answers without keeping the whole Translation in your working memory.

How you know you need to do this

sections.html:
Instructions

  1. Identify all the LR question stem types and their associated Back Up Plans in a section*.

    1. For instance, after reading a Weaken question stem, say, "Weaken. Does this make the conclusion less likely to be true?"

    2. Do not look at the stimulus or answer choices.

    3. This is not the time to attempt to answer the question.

  2. Go to the LSAT Question Database to check your question stem identifications.

  3. On the stems you get wrong, write down(on your scratch paper or using this template):

    1. The exact text of the stem you misidentified

    2. Your wrong question stem identification

    3. The correct question stem identification

    4. How you could know the correct identification next time

  4. Review the stems you misidentified and how you could identify them correctly before every Question Stem Training workout.

  5. Only stop Question Stem Training once you can reliably hit 100% question type and Back Up Plan identification accuracy on three sections in a row.
